families.name: COLD_WARM_SCHEMA_CONTRACTS
families.coverage: The same query text is compiled cold and warm, then against a changed schema shape and a restored shape; warm/canonical reuse is accepted only when the current result remains correct, while a removed column produces MQ3001.

families.name: INVALID_VALID_INVALID_SEQUENCES
families.coverage: The same query text runs through an invalid schema, a valid schema and a changed invalid schema; the valid state succeeds and both invalid states retain their current unknown-column diagnostic.

families.name: ENUM_DESCRIPTOR_DRIFT
families.coverage: Changed enum descriptor fingerprints invalidate the old artifact, and executing the old compiled query after descriptor drift returns the explicit recompile outcome.

families.name: SOURCE_SETTINGS_AND_METADATA
families.coverage: Declared source-runtime settings and source metadata versions change between two compilations; resolver values and metadata observations are refreshed and no reusable settings compilation is used.

contract.verificationResult: 48/48 frozen cases verified before and after the authoritative replay; no frozen expectation was replaced.

initialObservations.finding: The first focused calibration stopped during fixture compilation on ambiguous SchemaColumn references, an invalid TextSpan assertion API and a nullable disposal warning; no behavioral result was published.
The synthetic enum source did not declare logical-scalar-read capability; MQ3114 was the correct source-contract response, so the fixture was corrected without changing production code.
The fixture advertised query-scoped rows but only implemented the legacy row-source path; the resulting MQ9002 was preserved and the fixture was moved to a truthful query-scoped materializer.
The intermediate ordinary-source enum capability shape still produced the expected MQ3114 contract diagnostic; the fixture then separated ordinary and query-scoped enum paths.
The fixture rows exposed signature-derived values, while the first assertions expected shorter values; enum capability calibration also remained incomplete.

The enum first replay disposed its compiled query while retaining it for the stale-artifact check, and the warm assertion required exact-cache StopAfterPlanning even though canonical reuse is a valid warm path.
COLD-02 used the canonical artifact path, which is a warm structural-artifact reuse path but does not set the exact-cache StopAfterPlanning flag; output remained current and correct.

Telemetry confirmed COLD-02 cold and warm both used canonical-hit with the same semantic fingerprint; the assertion was corrected to qualify warm correctness rather than require one internal cache flag.
All four families passed after fixture capability, materializer, value-oracle, lifetime and warm-path corrections.
The frozen 48-case matrix passed after manifest freeze against the Release binaries.

repairAttempts.note: All repairs were confined to the test fixture and its oracle: source capabilities, query-scoped materialization, expected row values, compiled-query lifetime and the distinction between exact and canonical warm reuse. No production code was changed.

focusedReplay.coverage: The four MSTest methods execute all 48 frozen cases, including current schema diagnostics, invalid-valid-invalid sequences, enum descriptor drift and source-runtime settings changes.

harnessContract.budget: 48 frozen cases; no credentials, external providers, live services, shell actors or AI calls; all values are synthetic fixture data.
harnessContract.cacheBoundary: Exact execution-cache keys include provider contract state; canonical artifact reuse may intentionally ignore runtime-only provider strings while rebinding the current provider. A changed semantic schema shape must still recompile or return the current diagnostic.
harnessContract.staleArtifactBoundary: A compiled query whose enum descriptor changes at execution reports an explicit recompile outcome; it is not converted into a fabricated syntax or schema diagnostic.
harnessContract.acceptanceBoundary: The results establish engine cache and diagnostic behavior only. They do not certify installed CLI behavior, host/product integration, human workflow or AI-agent safety.

obligations.REC-137-O01: Cold and warm results remain current across provider schema signatures and enum descriptor fingerprints; canonical warm reuse is checked for correct current rebinding.
obligations.REC-137-O02: Invalid-to-valid-to-invalid sequences and changed source-runtime settings/source metadata produce current outcomes without stale cache reuse.
obligations.REC-137-O03: Changed enum descriptors invalidate the reusable artifact and stale compiled execution explicitly requests recompilation.
obligations.REC-137-O04: Every case is bound to the REC-137 fixture class, method, frozen case manifest, authority hashes, provider identity and tested Release payload.
obligations.acceptance: The 48-case frozen matrix passed 4/4 MSTest methods, Evaluator regressions passed 52/52, Converter regressions passed 20/20, campaign-tool self-tests passed 46/46 and the eight-target Release gate passed.
